result.topic_en: Corollaries on quadratic residues modulo a prime P = 2n+1: they coincide with even powers of a primitive root, there are exactly n of them, and the remaining n nonzero numbers are non-residues.
result.transcription:
110 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
Coroll. 1.
52. Reſidua ergo, quae ex diuiſione quadratorum per diuiſorem primum P naſcuntur, conuenient cum iis reſiduis, quae ex hac progreſſione geometrica naſcuntur
$1,\ a^2,\ a^4,\ a^6,\ a^8,\ a^{10},\ a^{12}$ etc.
exiſtente $a$ radice primitiua.
Coroll. 2.
53. Si ergo diuiſor primus ſit $P = 2n + 1$, quam formam omnes numeri primi praeter binarium habent, quia 2 non eſt numerus primus ad $P - 1 = 2n$, etiam $a^2$ non erit radix primitiua, ideoque ſeries reſiduorum ex quadratis oriunda non erit completa.
Coroll. 3.
54. Quia autem $a^{2n}$ eſt minima poteſtas radicis $a$ vnitatem relinquens, multitudo reſiduorum, quae ex numeris quadratis reſultare poſſunt, certo eſt $= n$, cyphra excluſa totidemque numeri nunquam poſſunt eſſe reſidua quadratorum, quos proinde non-reſidua appellaui.
Scholion 1.
55. Hoc etiam ex ſerie reſiduorum completa facillime perſpicitur, quae ſi progreſſioni geometricae ſubſcripta fuerint
$1,\ a,\ a^2,\ a^3,\ a^4,\ a^5,\ a^6,\ a^7 \ldots\ldots a^{2n}$
$1,\ \alpha,\ \beta,\ \gamma,\ \delta,\ \varepsilon,\ \zeta,\ \eta \ldots\ldots 1$ ex

items.quote:
Reſidua ergo, quae ex diuiſione quadratorum per diuiſorem primum P naſcuntur, conuenient cum iis reſiduis, quae ex hac progreſſione geometrica naſcuntur
$1,\ a^2,\ a^4,\ a^6,\ a^8,\ a^{10},\ a^{12}$ etc.
exiſtente $a$ radice primitiua.
items.english: Therefore the residues arising from dividing squares by the prime divisor P agree with the residues arising from the geometric progression 1, a^2, a^4, a^6, a^8, a^10, a^12 etc., where a is a primitive root.

items.quote: Si ergo diuiſor primus ſit $P = 2n + 1$, quam formam omnes numeri primi praeter binarium habent, quia 2 non eſt numerus primus ad $P - 1 = 2n$, etiam $a^2$ non erit radix primitiua, ideoque ſeries reſiduorum ex quadratis oriunda non erit completa.
items.english: If the prime divisor is P = 2n+1, a form all primes except 2 have, then since 2 is not prime to P-1 = 2n, a^2 will not be a primitive root, and so the series of residues arising from squares will not be complete.

items.quote: multitudo reſiduorum, quae ex numeris quadratis reſultare poſſunt, certo eſt $= n$, cyphra excluſa totidemque numeri nunquam poſſunt eſſe reſidua quadratorum
items.english: The number of residues that can arise from square numbers is certainly n, zero excluded, and equally many numbers can never be residues of squares (called non-residues).
